title: Here's What the Fed's Interest Rate Hike Means for Costco, Walmart, and Target (and My Top Pick to Buy Now)
author: Adria Cimino
description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter-point to combat inflation, which may reduce consumer spending power through higher credit card APRs, loan rates, and mortgage costs. However, value-focused retailers like Costco, Walmart, Target, and Amazon may benefit as cost-conscious consumers shift spending toward these companies known for competitive pricing and strong supply chains. The analyst views any weakness in these quality retailers as a buying opportunity.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong value-focused business model with bulk buying strategy enables rock-bottom pricing, positioning it to attract cost-conscious consumers during periods of higher interest rates and reduced spending power.
Well-structured supply chain and sourcing methods support low prices, making it an attractive destination for consumers seeking value during economic headwinds from rising rates.
Vast selection of owned brands helps maintain low costs and competitive pricing, positioning the retailer to benefit from consumers prioritizing value during periods of higher borrowing costs.

Identified as the analyst's top pick due to strong e-commerce value proposition combined with a booming cloud computing business benefiting from AI boom, offering both stability and growth potential despite near-term consumer spending pressures.

title: 1 Incredible Reason to Buy Costco Stock Before It Reports Earnings on Sept. 24.
author: Rick Munarriz
description: Costco is set to report fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on September 24, with strong sales growth of 11.3% already reported. The article highlights that investors should watch for signals of a record special dividend, as Costco has historically declared substantial one-time dividends every two to three years, with the last occurring in late 2023. While the company maintains a 22-year streak of regular dividend increases, the special distributions represent the real payoff for shareholders.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong net sales growth of 11.3% to $93.9 billion with robust 10.7% comparable store growth. The article anticipates a record special dividend announcement, supported by the company's historical pattern of declaring substantial one-time distributions every 2-3 years. The company has maintained 22 consecutive years of dividend increases, demonstrating financial strength and shareholder-friendly capital allocation.

title: TGT vs. COST: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
author: Na
description: Target (TGT) emerges as the superior value option compared to Costco (COST) based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook. TGT holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 15.32 and Value grade of B, while COST has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 39.73 and Value grade of D.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Target demonstrates stronger value characteristics with a higher Zacks Rank (#2 Buy vs #3 Hold), lower forward P/E ratio (15.32 vs 39.73), lower PEG ratio (2.52 vs 3.75), and a better Value grade (B vs D). The improving earnings estimate revision activity supports a positive outlook.

Costco receives a neutral sentiment as it is rated as a Hold with less attractive valuation metrics compared to Target. While not negative, the higher P/E ratio, PEG ratio, and lower Value grade suggest it is less undervalued at current price levels.

title: Better Buy for Cautious Investors: Eli Lilly vs Costco
author: Adria Cimino
description: The article compares Eli Lilly and Costco as defensive stock picks for cautious investors amid market hesitation. Eli Lilly benefits from its dominant GLP-1 weight loss drug portfolio (Mounjaro and Zepbound), while Costco offers stability through its membership-based business model with high renewal rates. Despite both stocks being reasonably valued, the author recommends Costco as the better buy, trading at approximately 39x forward earnings compared to Eli Lilly's historical valuation levels.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong growth driven by dominant GLP-1 weight loss drug portfolio (60% U.S. market share), generating over $14 billion in quarterly revenue. Expected continued growth as weight loss drug market projected to reach nearly $100 billion by decade's end. Diversified product portfolio provides revenue stability across market environments.

Recommended as the better cautious buy due to attractive valuation at 39x forward earnings (below historical levels). Defensive business model with high customer loyalty, membership renewal rates exceeding 90%, high-margin membership fees, and special dividends. Provides revenue visibility and stability during economic uncertainty.
